record.tranche_reason: The study compares superposition-related representation proxies under baseline and active-learning training, using different measures from the original toy-model work. It does not directly test feature packing geometry or its proposed causes.
record.gate_note: The study reports class-cluster, cosine-similarity, and activation-maximization results that it interprets as superposition. These are indirect proxies, not measurements of feature directions, feature sparsity, feature importance, or feature count relative to dimensions. No separately extractable figure-only values are included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares baseline and least-confidence active-learning ResNet-18 models on class-cluster overlap (t-SNE, silhouette, Davies-Bouldin), cosine similarity of feature vectors, and activation-maximization images, and calls the differences 'superposition'. None of these measure what any version names: feature directions relative to dimension count, sparsity, feature importance, neuron polysemanticity, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality. Class separability is a related but different construct, so the study does not test any version. It records its findings under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that active learning performed worse on both datasets and 'seems to have more Superposition', citing cluster overlap and cosine statistics. They call for examining how data picking affects representations. The paraphrase omits one point: the authors claim the cosine statistics support more superposition even though Tiny ImageNet mean cosine similarity was lower under active learning.
record.recipe_differences: The original work studies toy models of feature superposition; this study trains ResNet-18 image classifiers on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet and compares baseline training with least-confidence active learning, using indirect clustering, cosine-similarity, and visualization measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary by dataset: active learning has higher mean cosine similarity on CIFAR-10 but lower mean cosine similarity on Tiny ImageNet. Clustering metrics and qualitative visualizations indicate worse separation for active learning on both datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Least-confidence active learning gave ResNet-18 worse class-cluster separation than baseline training on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet. Silhouette fell from 0.212 to 0.189 and from -0.348 to -0.399. Mean cosine similarity rose on CIFAR-10 (0.885 to 0.927) but fell on Tiny ImageNet (0.310 to 0.254). The authors interpret this as more superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-data selection (uncertainty-based active learning) changes class-cluster separability of learned representations in image CNNs. Whether this reflects superposition is not established by these proxies.

record.problems: Superposition is inferred from indirect proxies rather than direct measurements of feature directions or neuron polysemanticity. The authors note that some unit visualizations are hard to interpret, and that Tiny ImageNet units from the two models are not directly comparable. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparse-feature vs dimension manipulation, no geometry or phase transition.
All: no measure of capacity, feature importance or polysemantic neurons.
All: polysemanticity is not measured, and no non-capacity cause is established.
All: these are CNN image classifiers, not LLMs, with no neuron-spread or SAE measures.
All: feature dimensionality is not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The record set relation 'tests'/T2. I reclassify it as discusses/T6 because every row measures class clustering or feature-vector similarity, not superposition as any version defines it. The study is a single-author preprint, with one run per condition, no uncertainty estimates and no controls. Its activation-maximization comparisons are acknowledged by the author as not directly comparable.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy-model feature packing, more sparse features than dimensions, near-orthogonal directions, or a sparsity-dependent transition.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not measure polysemantic neurons or establish a non-capacity cause of polysemanticity.
Uses ResNet-18 image classifiers, not LLMs; does not measure feature spread across neurons or SAE recovery.
Does not study SAE features or their completeness, stability, or canonical status.
Does not measure the dimensionality of represented features.
